cards.title: Introduction to State Management
cards.content: State management is the practice of sharing and managing data across multiple components in an application. In smaller Vue applications, passing props and emitting events is sufficient, but larger apps require a centralized store.

options.text: Passing data efficiently through a global store.
Passing props through multiple nested components just to reach a deeply nested child.
A method to optimize database queries.

cards.title: Meet Pinia
cards.content:
Pinia is the official, recommended state management library for Vue 3. It provides a modular, type-safe, and intuitive API inspired by Vuex but with a much lighter footprint and zero boilerplate.

import { defineStore } from 'pinia';

export const useCounterStore = defineStore('counter', {
  state: () => ({ count: 0 }),
  actions: {
    increment() { this.count++; }
  }
});

cards.title: Using Stores in Components
cards.content:
Using a Pinia store inside a Vue component is straightforward. You simply import your store hook, call it inside your setup function or script setup, and access its properties directly.

<script setup>
import { useCounterStore } from '@/stores/counter';
const counter = useCounterStore();
</script>

<template>
  <button @click="counter.increment()">{{ counter.count }}</button>
</template>

cards.title: Conclusion
cards.content: You have mastered the basics of state management with Pinia in Vue.js! Remember to use Pinia for shared global state, leverage getters for computed derived data, and keep actions responsible for business logic.
